Nodes: color, size, shape and labels

Source: R/mira_pieces.R
mira_node.Rd

Maps node color and size to node attributes (color_by, size_by), or sets them to constants (color, size, shape), and shows node names. Add it to a plot made with mira(). Anything not given keeps MiRA's default.

Usage

mira_node(
  color_by,
  color,
  size_by,
  size,
  shape,
  labels,
  label_size,
  perspective,
  color_values,
  color_scale,
  highlight,
  color_palette,
  color_reverse,
  color_limits
)

Arguments

color_by

Column to color nodes by: a node or state-node column (e.g. "module") or a MiRA-computed attribute (e.g. "intra_degree_sum"). ".set" colors by set membership (bipartite networks). NULL or NA = MiRA's default.

color

A constant node color: a color name ("red") or "#rrggbb". Give color_by or color, not both. Colors are opaque: the transparency of a color such as "#ff000080" is ignored, with a warning (here and in every other color argument).

size_by

Numeric column to size nodes by. NULL or NA = default.

size

Base node size, a whole number between 3 and 25 (10 = MiRA's default).

shape

"circle", "square", "triangle" or "diamond". Every shape has the circle's area, so node sizes stay comparable.

labels

TRUE or FALSE: show node names.

label_size

Node name size, a whole number between 8 and 24 (12 = MiRA's default). Used when node names are shown.

perspective

TRUE or FALSE: draw nodes in the layers' 3D perspective (MiRA's default) or flat.

color_values

Colors for values of the color_by column, named by value: c("1" = "red", "3" = "#1f77b4"). Values not listed keep MiRA's palette. Gives a categorical scale. Per set: list(pollinator = c(...)). With color_by = ".set", the colors of the sets: c(pollinator = "red", plant = "green"). See mira_scales.

color_scale

"categorical" (one color per value) or "continuous" (a gradient; numeric columns only). Without it, MiRA decides from the data. Per set: c(pollinator = "continuous"). See mira_scales.

highlight

A node name: the node and its neighbors stand out in every layer and the rest is dimmed, as when the node is picked in MiRA's Search Node. The banner "Selected node" clears it.

color_palette

A named palette for the color_by scale: a categorical one ("Okabe-Ito", "Set1", ...) gives one color per value, a continuous one ("magma", "RdBu", ...) a gradient. Names are matched without case; the list is in mira_scales. Per set: c(pollinator = "magma").

color_reverse

TRUE reverses the palette. Per set: c(pollinator = TRUE).

color_limits

c(min, max): the gradient runs from min to max instead of the data's range, so several plots can share one scale; values outside take the end colors. Gives a continuous scale. Per set: list(pollinator = c(0, 10)).

Value

A component, to add to a plot with +.

Details

Per set. On a bipartite network (mira(..., bipartite = TRUE)), color_by, size_by, shape, color_scale, color_palette and color_reverse also take a vector named by the node_type values, giving each set its own setting, e.g. color_by = c(pollinator = "module", plant = NA); color_values and color_limits take a list named the same way, list(pollinator = c("1" = "red")). A set that is not named keeps MiRA's default, and a later per-set value replaces an earlier one whole: name both sets in one call. The scale settings of the two sets differ only when the sets are colored by different attributes, because MiRA keeps one scale per attribute name (mira_scales). When color or size is per set and shape is not given, MiRA draws one set as circles and the other as squares.

Computed attributes. MiRA computes each node's degree (its number of links) and strength (the sum of their weights), within layers (intra_) and between layers (inter_, when the network has interlayer links). For each node in each layer (a state node): intra_degree, intra_strength, inter_degree, inter_strength. For each node over all its layers, their sum and their mean: intra_degree_sum, intra_degree_mean, and so on. On a directed network the names carry the direction instead: intra_in_degree, intra_out_degree, intra_in_strength_sum, ... R warns when a name is not computed for the network, and suggests the ones that are; mira_options() lists them.

Columns that cannot be mapped. MiRA does not offer the columns that identify the rows: node_id, node_name, layer_id, layer_name and layers_present for nodes; layer_from, node_from, layer_to, node_to, weight and directed for links; layer_id, bipartite, latitude and longitude for layers. To map one, copy it to a column of another name (net$layers$lat <- net$layers$latitude).

See also

mira_scales for color_values, color_scale and sizes; mira() for how components combine.

Other components: mira_camera(), mira_filter(), mira_interlayer(), mira_intralayer(), mira_layer(), mira_layout(), mira_legends(), mira_mode, mira_mode_dashboard(), mira_mode_data(), mira_mode_grid(), mira_mode_layer(), mira_mode_map(), mira_mode_meta()

Examples

library(emln)
net <- load_emln(17) # 4 layers; bird and plant nodes
#> Creating state node map
#> Creating extended link list with node IDs
p <- mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird")
#> Bipartite network: drawn as undirected. Use directed = TRUE for a directed one.

# Map color and size to attributes
p + mira_node(color_by = "verification_level", size_by = "intra_degree_sum")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Constants
p + mira_node(color = "steelblue", size = 8, shape = "triangle")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# One setting per node set
p + mira_node(color_by = c(bird = "intra_degree_sum", plant = NA),
              shape = c(bird = "diamond", plant = "circle"))
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Node names; flat nodes
p + mira_node(labels = TRUE, label_size = 10, perspective = FALSE)
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Highlight a node and its neighbors
p + mira_node(highlight = "Geospiza_fortis")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Choose the colors (see ?mira_scales)
p + mira_node(color_by = "verification_level",
              color_values = c(species = "#1f77b4", genus = "orange"))
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
p + mira_node(color_by = "intra_degree_sum", color_scale = "categorical")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
